<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par160 />{{GHGmargin-letter|160|c}}
(''c'') By the preposition {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}} governing a complete noun-clause, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=עַל לֹֽא־חָמָס בְּכַפָּ֑י|translate=notwithstanding}} that ''no violence is in mine hands'', or a verbal-clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=9}}. On {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}} with the infinitive in a similar sense (equivalent to ''in addition to the fact'' that = ''notwithstanding'' that), cf. {{GHGpar|119|aa}}, note 2.<section end=par160 />

<section begin=par161 />{{GHGpar-heading|161|Comparative Clauses}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|161|a}}
'''1.''' A comparison between two facts is sometimes established by simply uniting them with {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}, especially in gnomic poetry, when facts of a moral nature are compared with those of the physical world, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=7}} ''man is born unto trouble, and the sons of flame fly upward'', i.e. as the sparks by nature fly upward, so man, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=11}} (in an interrogative form; in 34:3 the same comparison as a statement); 14:11 f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, 9, 14, 27:21, &c.<ref>On this {{GHGterm|wāw adaequationis}}, and in general on these proverbial comparisons, see Delitzsch, ''Das Salomonische Spruchbuch'', p. 9 f. Moreover, instead of entire clauses, the nouns alone (without predicates) are frequently grouped together, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=21|hidebook=1}} (called by Delitzsch, the ‘emblematic Mashal’). The expressions {{GHGheb|text=נֶחְשַׁב עִם}} prop. ''to be counted with some one'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=88|verse=5}}, and {{GHGheb|text=נִמְשַׁל עִם|translate=to be likened with some one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=28|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=143|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, also arise from the idea of comparison implied in grouping things together. On this use of {{GHGheb|text=עִם}} cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=26}}, where ''with'' is equivalent to ''like''.</ref> Even without the connecting {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=19}} ''drought and heat consume the snow waters'', {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאוֹל חָטָ֫אוּ}} so doth ''Sheol'' those who ''have sinned'' (cf. {{GHGpar|155|n}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=11}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|161|b}}
'''2.''' The conjunction {{GHGheb|text=כַּֽאֲשֶׁר}} (cf. {{GHGpar|155|g}}; the simple {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} occurs in the same sense in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=18|hidebook=1}}) ''as'', ''quemadmodum'', is used as a comparative conjunction ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=15}}), frequently with {{GHGheb|text=כֵּן|translate=so}}, corresponding to it in the apodosis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=14|hidebook=1}} f. Sometimes, however, {{GHGheb|text=כֵּן}} (''so also'') occurs even after independent statements, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=20}}.—Exact coincidence of two facts is expressed in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=15}} by {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־עֻמַּת שָׁ·}}<ref>In spite of its form this particle has originally nothing to do with {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־|translate=all}}. The expression is compounded of {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} and {{GHGheb|text=לְעֻמַּת}}, like the Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־קֳבֵל}} for {{GHGheb|text=כְּלָֽקֳבֵל}}; cf. M. Lambert, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xxx. 47.</ref> ''in all points as''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|161|c}}
Rem. On the use of {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍|translate=as}}, with single nouns or pronouns to introduce comparisons, cf. 118 ''s''; on the alleged use of {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} as a conjunction (equivalent to {{GHGheb|text=כַּֽאֲשֶׁר}}), cf. {{GHGpar|155|g}}.—It is to be further remarked that {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}—{{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} when used in correspondence with one another, ''as—so'' (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=4|verse=9}}; also ''so—as'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=4}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=14|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=30|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּ}}—{{GHGheb|text=וּכְ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=127|verse=4}} and often, {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}—{{GHGheb|text=כֵּן}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=4}}), are not to be regarded as conjunctions, but as virtual substantives with a following genitive; {{GHGheb|text=כָּכֶם כַּגֵּר יִֽהְיֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=15|verse=15}} properly means ''the like of you shall be the like of the stranger'', i.e. ''your duty shall be'' (also) ''the stranger’s duty''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=22}}.<section end=par161 /><noinclude>
